title: Decision: should triage grade cards against a launch critical-path list?
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cxgb3PKFkt8y5FigJn

## 维护者速读

- 问题:现在卡的级只看缺陷多严重、多少人碰到,不看它在不在上线演示要走的那条路上;路上的阻塞缺陷如果只有管理员碰到,就排在本专题里等,不会插队。
- 选项:A 按上线清单重新定级,路上的先做,路外的全部降到最低一档、只在收尾时顺带做;A2 只升不降,路上的阻塞和错数据升到插队一档,其余卡的级不动,清单同时当作派活次序;B 规则不变,靠你逐张点名;C 等有上线日期再议。
- 推荐 A2:上线阻塞一样先修,而用户看得见的路外缺陷不会被悄悄搁置。
- 不定会怎样:照现在的规则走,上线路上只有管理员碰到的阻塞缺陷可能排到上线之后。

## Decision asked

Whether triage adds a launch/demo critical-path list (5–10 items, supplied by you) as an input to the grade (p1/p2/p3), and if so whether it may only raise grades or also lower them. Ordering inside one grade is unchanged.

## Today

Grading rules live in `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, "Priority" items 2–3; the skill only executes them (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/filing-gate.md`: "表 ⛔ 本文不抄").

- Grade = severity crossed with reach. Broken means "a core feature of the area table cannot be done, and there is no workaround". The "Product areas" table is already a standing critical-path list.
- "UX has no p3": a UX problem on a core feature every user hits every time is p1, every other one p2.
- "A paused area no longer demotes its cards to p3: the grade reflects severity, not whether the area is being dispatched."
- "A card is not re-graded card by card: one re-grade pass when these grading rules change, none otherwise; a card in flight ... may be raised, never lowered."
- "The grade only decides whether a card jumps the queue; what is dispatched is decided by the area ... in the order of the areas and sub-epics the maintainer names." p1 jumps every area, paused ones included.
- p1 inflation check exists: "Triage reads the open p1 cards once a week, and when there are more than ten re-checks whether they were graded too high."
- Pick order, unchanged by this card (`references/execution-duties.md`): "取卡全序:维护者直派插队卡,契约面卡,标签序" (the skill joins the three with a greater-than sign) and "同级先非车队卡 ..., 再 `Bug`、卡龄": maintainer-named, contract cards, non-fleet before fleet, bugs, oldest.
- p3: "p3 left for the close-out or batched" (North Star); "p3 留收口或搭同文件 PR 成批(每 PR ≤5 卡)" (`references/area-lease.md`).
- Human-set grades are never moved; a seat objects with a one-line comment (`filing-gate.md`). Seats already send `Suggested-grade:` lines that triage confirms or overrules (`references/triage-duties.md`).

## Proposal

As drafted: on the path and blocks users or produces wrong data → p1; on the path, UX only → p2; off the path → p3. One-line rationale in the triage comment ("path: demo-approval · wrong data"). New or changed cards re-graded as they arrive, the whole backlog when the list changes. Weekly 5-card spot-check; seats may appeal with evidence; no new labels.

Where it collides with today's text:

1. "Off the path → p3" makes the grade encode focus instead of severity, which the paused-area sentence rules out, and it breaks "UX has no p3".
2. "On the path, UX only → p2" lowers UX problems on core features that are p1 today.
3. A full re-grade per list change contradicts "not re-graded card by card"; in-flight and human-set grades cannot be lowered anyway.
4. The spot-check and the appeal duplicate the weekly p1 read and the `Suggested-grade:` / one-line objection channels.
5. Security and data-wrong cards are graded by their own tables and "do not wait for the road"; off the path they must keep their grade.
6. The list is a current value: `filing-gate.md` keeps those in project memory, not in skill text. Only the rule sentence is standing.

## Costs and risks

- Demotion to p3 means off-path cards are no longer dispatched on their own: they wait for the close-out or a same-file PR.
- Every list edit triggers a pass over the whole open backlog (A only).
- p1 jumps every area, so each card raised to p1 delays the area in progress. A loose list inflates p1.

## Options

- **A. Adopt as drafted (raise and lower).** Launch-path bugs go first. Every off-path p2, including visible UX defects and builder-facing bugs, drops to the close-out and may not ship before launch. Needs three North Star sentences rewritten.
- **A2. Raise-only.** One added sentence in "Priority" item 2: a Broken or data-wrong Bug on a listed path item is p1 whatever its reach column. Nothing is lowered. You name the list as the dispatch order (the existing "areas and sub-epics the maintainer names" lever), so on-path p2 cards are taken before other areas' p2. Launch-path blockers and wrong data jump the queue; on-path UX comes next; off-path p2 keeps its grade and is done later, not parked; off-path p1 still jumps. Only cards on listed items are re-read.
- **B. Keep current rules only.** No grading change. Launch cards are done sooner only if you name them or their area first; an on-path Broken bug with admin or rare reach stays p2 and waits its area turn.
- **C. Defer.** Same as B until a launch date exists; revisit then.

## Recommendation

A2. It puts launch blockers first with one sentence, keeps the grade meaning severity, and needs no backlog-wide re-grade or new check: the weekly p1 read already catches inflation. A is not recommended because its main effect beyond A2 is demotion, which contradicts three standing sentences and silently parks user-visible defects. Gap: no count yet of cards A would demote or A2 would raise; triage can produce it once the list exists.

## Four facets

os-decision-facets
- ① Long-term soundness: A2 adds one raise-only sentence and keeps the grade meaning severity; A adds a second meaning (focus) to the grade and rewrites three standing sentences, a growing special case.
- ② Business pull: real once a launch or demo date exists, since on-path blockers with administrator or rare reach wait their area turn today; with no date there is no pull, which is option C.
- ③ Preventing AI mistakes: a closed list of 5–10 named path items with a one-line rationale is checkable by any seat; A lets a seat park a user-visible defect silently by reading it as off-path, A2 cannot lower anything.
- ④ No sprawl at startup stage: no new label, gate or check under A2 (the weekly p1 read already exists); A adds a per-list-change backlog pass, a spot-check and an appeal path that duplicate existing ones.

Prior rulings read: priority,grade,triage,p1,p3 → 14 hits; none; thread: none

The 14 hits are ADR-0029, 0056, 0060, 0069 and 0076 decisions that use these words for product fields and status triage; none rules on card grading. The card is not filed yet, so there is no thread to read.

Self-check: on facet ① alone the choice is A2; ②③④ do not flip it.

## What you supply if A or A2

1. The list: 5–10 path items, each one line, ideally rows of the "Product areas" table.
2. The launch or demo date, so the list has an end and raised cards return to their table grade afterwards.
3. For A only: confirmation that off-path UX and builder bugs may drop to p3.
